blockingLoop.evidence: Pulley/melted-plastic check asked in turn 2 and again in turn 4 after customer said 'dont know about anything else tbh'

rationale: The assistant correctly reasoned to the hidden truth: hair/tassel jam caused the drive belt to overheat and snap, and it sensibly got the model number U85-AS-Be. However it rigidly insisted on a qualified engineer every turn ('Do not use the vacuum again, even with a replacement belt fitted') for what the ground truth treats as a routine user-level belt change with no electrical smell or sparks, matching the listed unsupported claim of an engineer-requiring fire risk. It never actually told the customer to obtain the correct belt despite having the model, and re-requested the same pulley inspection after the customer indicated they could not say more, so the homeowner leaves with a correct cause but no actionable fix.
